subject: humanities
passage: The Impressionists are often described as rebels shut out by the art world of nineteenth-century Paris. According to this account, the official Salon, the city's most important exhibition, rejected their loose brushwork and everyday subjects, so the painters had no choice but to organize their own independent show in 1874.
passage_b: Art historian Odile Marchand points out that the story is less tidy than it seems. Several future Impressionists, including Claude Monet and Pierre-Auguste Renoir, had paintings accepted by the Salon in the 1860s. Their rejections were real but inconsistent, and Marchand argues that the 1874 exhibition reflected a wish to show their work on their own terms as much as a lack of other options.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the account in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that the Salon accepted nearly every painting the Impressionists sent in
choices.B: By agreeing that the painters held their own show only because the Salon refused them
choices.C: By noting that some of the painters had earlier found success at the Salon
choices.D: By claiming that the Impressionists' brushwork was less loose than critics believed

explanation.why: Text 1 says the painters "had no choice" but to hold their own show because the Salon rejected them. Text 2 notes that Monet and Renoir "had paintings accepted by the Salon in the 1860s" and calls the rejections "real but inconsistent." So the author of Text 2 would complicate the account by pointing to these earlier successes.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says the rejections "were real," so it does not claim the Salon accepted nearly everything.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 argues that the 1874 show reflected a wish to show work "on their own terms" as much as a lack of options, so it does not agree with "only."
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 points out that several future Impressionists had paintings accepted by the Salon, which complicates the story of total exclusion.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 does not discuss the painters' brushwork.
